title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Let X_1 = R^2/Z^2 be the torus and U_{1,1} = X_1 minus the image of the origin, the once-punctured torus. Its fundamental group pi_{1,1} is free on two generators x, y. The previous page gives the presentation pi_{1,1} = <x, y, l_0' | [x,y] l_0' = 1>, where l_0' is the loop around the puncture. The group ST_{1,1}, a covering of GL(2,Z), is identified with the normaliser in Aut_loc(pi_{1,1}) of the inertia subgroup L generated by l_0'. Grothendieck wants to write explicitly how the generators rho, sigma, tau' (or r_0, r_1, r_infty) act on x and y. Each generator should send l_0' to l_0' or to l_0'^{-1}.

What this page does. To make the generators x, y concrete, he passes to the Z^2-covering R^2 \ Z^2 -> U_{1,1}. This is the restriction of the universal covering R^2 -> X_1.
- He chooses a base point a in R^2 \ Z^2 lying over the base point a_{1,1}. This gives a canonical isomorphism (42): pi_{1,1} = the 'mixed' fundamental group pi_1(R^2 \ Z^2, Z^2; a). This is the fundamental group of the quotient of R^2 \ Z^2 by the free, properly discontinuous action of Z^2.
- Hence the exact sequence (43): 1 -> pi_1(R^2 \ Z^2) -> pi_{1,1} -> Z^2 -> 1. Here pi_1(R^2 \ Z^2) is free of infinite rank and equals the commutator subgroup. Also Z^2 = pi_1(X_1) = (pi_{1,1})^{ab}.
- Following 'Jean Malgoire's calculus', elements of the mixed pi_1 are the pairs (44) (gamma, l). Here gamma is in Z^2 and l is a homotopy class of paths in R^2 \ Z^2 from a to a+gamma. Composition is (gamma, l)(gamma', l') = (gamma+gamma', l followed by (gamma-translate of l')).
- With a = (1/2, 1/2) (45), x and y are defined as the lifts of the basis vectors e_0, e_1 given by the straight segments from a to a+e_0, resp. a+e_1.
- Then xyx^{-1}y^{-1} is the boundary of a unit square with corners a, a+e_0, a+e_0+e_1, a+e_1, which contains exactly one lattice point. The figure is drawn so that this point is the origin o. This boundary is visibly opposite to the direct (counterclockwise) straight loop from a around o.
- Hence [x,y] = l_0'^{-1}, i.e. [x,y] l_0' = 1, consistent with presentation (40).

Purpose. This normalisation is the first step toward writing the action of the lifted GL(2,Z) on F_2 = pi_{1,1}. The idea is that a matrix acts linearly on R^2, preserving Z^2 and the origin, and one transports (gamma, l) to (A gamma, A(l)), corrected by a path from A a back to a. This explicitly realises Nielsen's classical picture: Aut(F_2) -> GL(2,Z) is onto, and automorphisms send [x,y] to a conjugate of [x,y]^{+-1}. It feeds the Teichmüller-tower / Galois-action programme of the Longue Marche (genus 1, one puncture).
errors: Minor labelling looseness: with e_0=(1,0), e_1=(0,1) and a=(1/2,1/2), the square a -> a+e_0 -> a+e_0+e_1 -> a+e_1 encloses (1,1), not the origin. The figure gets the origin inside by orienting e_0, e_1 differently, with vertex labels a+e_1, a+e_0, a-e_0-e_1(?) that are hard to read. This is harmless, since all lattice points map to the single puncture and the commutator is a well-defined element. But the vertex labels in the figure are not fully consistent.

Orientation: the text (read correctly as 'opposé') gives [x,y] = (direct loop)^{-1}, consistent with (40) [x,y] l_0' = 1 when l_0' is the direct loop. No error, provided one reads 'opposé' rather than 'homotope'.

ideas.what: Fundamental group of a quotient by a free proper Z^2-action described as pairs (group element, path class from a to its translate), the 'π_1 mixte'.
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental group of a quotient / orbifold (or stack) [Y/G]; the extension 1 -> π_1(Y) -> π_1([Y/G]) -> G -> 1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (covering space theory); in Grothendieck's school the 'π_1 mixte'; here attributed to Jean Malgoire's calculus
ideas.where_published: Mixed fundamental groups occur in Grothendieck's Galois-theoretic writings (SGA1 circle, Longue Marche); unsure of a precise reference. Malgoire's own write-up is unknown to me.

ideas.what: Exact sequence identifying the free group of infinite rank π_1(R^2 \ Z^2) with the commutator subgroup of F_2 = π_{1,1}, with quotient Z^2 = π_1(torus) = abelianisation.
ideas.modern_name: Commutator subgroup of F_2 as π_1 of the maximal abelian cover of the punctured torus

ideas.what: Normalised choice of generators x, y as straight-segment lifts from a = (1/2,1/2), so that [x,y] is the inverse of the straight loop around a lattice point. This prepares an explicit GL(2,Z)~ action on F_2 normalising the inertia subgroup.
ideas.modern_name: Nielsen's theorem / mapping class group of the once-punctured torus acting on F_2; inertia preserved up to inversion
ideas.where_published: The Teichmüller tower (M_{1,1}, SL_2(Z)) appears in Esquisse d'un programme; this explicit computation, not to my knowledge

missed.claim: Historical detail: Grothendieck credits a 'calcul de Jean Malgoire' for explicit computation in mixed fundamental groups via pairs (γ, ℓ). This documents Malgoire's contribution to the Montpellier Galois–Teichmüller work, which is little recorded in the literature.
missed.quote: Les éléments du π_1 mixte s'explicitent par le calcul de Jean Malgoire à l'aide des couples (γ, ℓ)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Attribution and history of the Montpellier school's contribution to the Longue Marche. The mathematics itself is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard covering-space description of π_1 of the punctured torus and a normalisation of generators. Mathematically routine; the only point of interest is the attribution to Jean Malgoire.
transcription_corrections: Near the end the image reads 'qui est visiblement opposé au lacet "rectiligne" direct de a autour de l'origine o', not 'homotope'. This fixes the sign: [x,y] = l_0'^{-1}, consistent with (40).
The crossed-out mark at top left is a struck-through equation number/label, not text.
The line before 'Nous prendrons' is a marginal or inserted remark, roughly 'Suivons "comme convenu" les fonctions' (uncertain). It is not 'prenons'.
The word struck through after 'Nous prendrons, au dessus des générateurs' is 'considérons les' (crossed out); the sentence continues with 'e_0, e_1 de Z^2'.
In (42) the notation π_1(R^2\Z^2, Z^2; a) denotes the mixed fundamental group (pairs (γ, ℓ)), not a relative π_1.
